answer: Trickle-Terrace Admission Control: each identity must sustain a minimum 30-day stream of small, irregularly spaced transactions before gaining full API weight. Traffic that rises in a smooth curve toward the limit is throttled, reserving capacity for bursty organic use. An attacker must pay to run thousands of identities through this slow ramp, then keep them active to hold weight, so cost scales with time, not just one-time registration.
